samples.question: This picture contains six separated grey-framed cards, spread far apart across the canvas. Each card carries three things: a coloured square in its top-left corner, which is that card's own address colour; a coloured square in its top-right corner, which is the address colour of the card this card forwards to; and a row of one, two or three small dark squares along its bottom, which is that card's pip tally. The six address colours are all different and are drawn from red, green, blue, purple, orange and teal. A solid dark triangle floats just above exactly one card, and that card is where the relay starts. The relay lands on four cards in total: it lands first on the card under the triangle, and then makes exactly three jumps, each jump going from the card it is on to the card whose top-left address colour matches that card's top-right forwarding colour. Count the pips on every card the relay lands on and add them up; pips on cards the relay never lands on do not count, and every plain mid-grey square or circle outside the cards is inert decoration that counts for nothing. What is the total number of pips on the four cards the relay lands on?
